newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil steady to soft in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil steady to soft in quiet trade.

text.p: NWE spot gas oil prices were steady to soft in quiet trade on Wednesday with good supplies keeping buyers relaxed, traders said.
"Even diesel sellers were struggling to find the buyers today," one said, referring to Tuesday's flurry of activity.
Early July diesel premiums were around July IPE +$6/+$6.50, slightly softer on the sell side.
Around six diesel cargoes were traded on Tuesday at premiums between July IPE +$5.50 and +$6.50 per tonne depending on date and delivery point, four into French ports and two into ARA.
Additionally an Algerian cargo was sold prompt into Antwerp at July +$6.75 a tonne.
0.2 percent sulphur premiums held a slightly wider range with the IPE contango of around $2 keeping buyers and sellers apart.

Prompt 0.2 sulphur was valued around July futures evens with good prompt supplies leaving buyers looking for discounts, while July 1-15 cargo bids were screen evens at best. Sellers, eyeing the futures contango looked for July IPE +$1 per tonne.
The ARA barge market for heating oil talked on a two-tier basis with tighter refinery supplies taking a small premium to storage material.
Prompt lifting storage barges were traded from July IPE -50 cents up to screen evens with a Rotterdam refinery barge taking July IPE +25 cents.
Amsterdam/Rotterdam liftings were valued around July screen evens in late business.
Antwerp and Flushing lifting diesel barges were assessed around July IPE +$4/+$5 with Rotterdam loadings asking +$6 a tonne.
